body:

Option (a) in full: "Parse them into rows: a circuit_paths table (circuit, step order, part, terminal, wire colour, fuse, ground, note) that the Diagrams page renders as the write-up read today; the Markdown files leave the tree; the wiring-diagram PDF stays in the ignored library as the source. title: Repository private, all rights reserved
body:
**The repository goes private and carries a LICENSE stating all rights reserved; the manuals stay where they are.**

Camden's answer to block 06.03 (2026-10-13, desktop): option (a), no words added. Option (a) in full: "Make the repository private, and state 'all rights reserved' in a LICENSE file. The manuals stay where they are, the phone keeps working through its token (the token becomes required for reading too), CI keeps running, nothing is rewritten. Nobody outside sees the record; a sponsor showcase would need a separate public face later."

Reasoning: the recommendation was (a); it stops the redistribution of copyrighted manuals without rewriting history (no force-push).

Consequences: a LICENSE file (all rights reserved) is added at the repository root in this pass; switching the repository to private is a GitHub setting only Camden can change (the tool cannot), and the phone's token must have read access to it. No manuals are moved or history rewritten; the intake's bulk still leaves git by parse row (T2).

title: Procedure steps are rows: a procedure_steps table in 00-CAR, shown by the Manual from the rows
body:
**A procedure parsed from a manual is rows, not a document: `00-CAR` gets a `procedure_steps` table (id `<procedure>.<two digits>`, procedure, n, do, how, expect, caution, page), one row per step, and the Manual shows a procedure's steps from those rows when it has no Markdown body.**

Decided by the agent (CLAUDE.md §3, small; nobody was asked): D-523 rules every procedure step into the car's tables and the parse rows say "one row per step", but `procedures` held only a heading and a Markdown body, and D-519 says a new document is not written. The columns are the ones `01-electrical`'s `steps` table already uses (D-533), so a step reads the same in both places; `page` is the page of the procedure's `source`.

In the tool: `export` gives each procedure its `steps` in order and, where there is no `data/procedures/<id>.md`, builds the body the app already renders from them - nothing in the app changes. The two hand-written procedures (PR-001, PR-002) keep their Markdown bodies until they are rewritten as steps.

A step is where a figure is used, never its home (R2): a figure in a step names the `specs` row that holds it, and another year's figure stays marked as such there.

Undoing this is deleting rows and one table declaration; nothing is bought, cut or wired.

title: Install poppler on the Mac so scanned manual pages can be read
body:
**The agent may install poppler on the Mac with Homebrew, so a run can read scanned manual pages as images.**

His answer, option (a): "Yes: the agent installs poppler on the Mac with Homebrew (brew install poppler). Free, about a minute, removed again with brew uninstall poppler. Scanned pages can then be read as images on the Mac. Forecloses nothing." No further words.

Reasoning: costs nothing, reversible with brew uninstall poppler, and unblocks drawings and mark tables (e.g. the 1985 maintenance table intervals, P83) that OCR text cannot give.

Consequences: poppler is installed on the Mac (pdftoppm available); scanned sections are parsed with the page looked at, not text alone; P83 and the drawings/mark tables skipped earlier may be re-taken by the plan run.

title: rx7.py add takes many rows from a file (--rows)
body:
**`rx7.py add` takes many rows from a file: `add AREA TABLE --rows FILE [col=value ...]`. The file's first line names the columns, every later line is one row split on `|` (`--sep` changes it), and the col=value pairs of the command line go on every row. Every row passes the same checks as a single `add`, and all are checked before any is written.**

Decided by the agent (CLAUDE.md §3, small; nobody was asked): D-523 rules every spec and procedure step of every manual into the car's tables, a section is some hundreds of rows, and `add` took one row per call. A run started from the app may run `rx7.py` and nothing else, so a scratch loader script is refused by the harness; the rows could only have gone in as hundreds of `add` calls joined in one command. §7 says calls are the cost.

Nothing about what a row must be changes: the declared columns, the types, the references and the key are checked by the code that checked them before (`value_problems`), a key that already exists or repeats in the file is refused, and a refusal writes nothing. Ids in the file are the next free ones of their table, read from the table before the file is written; `new` and `block` still issue every D- and block id.

In the tool: `rows_from_file` reads the file, `cmd_add` checks and writes; three selftests cover the reader.

Undoing this is deleting one option from the tool; nothing is bought, cut or wired.
